short: A robust British fighter that bore the brunt of the air combat and scored the majority of kills during the Battle of Britain.
full:
Introduced in 1937, the Hawker Hurricane was the Royal Air Force's first modern monoplane fighter, incorporating an enclosed cockpit and retractable undercarriage. Unlike the Spitfire, its fuselage retained a traditional fabric-covered tubular structure, which made it easier to manufacture and remarkably resilient to battle damage. During the Battle of Britain, Hurricane squadrons outnumbered Spitfires and were responsible for over sixty percent of the German aircraft destroyed in the campaign.

While it was eventually outclassed in the pure air superiority role in Europe by advanced Axis fighters, the Hurricane was adapted for other vital tasks. It served extensively as a fighter-bomber, famously armed with heavy cannons for anti-tank duties in North Africa, and as a carrier-capable naval fighter guarding vital Atlantic convoys. By the end of the conflict, over fourteen thousand had been built.
